record.original_question: For standard arithmetic functions such as the sum of divisors sigma(n), the prime-counting function J(x), the number of distinct prime factors, the divisor-counting function d(n), and the largest prime factor p(n), determine the least number of iterations needed to force specified threshold or terminal behaviors, and ask for analogous results for related variants such as sigma_r(n), J(x; a, b), and other arithmetic functions.

evidence.quote: Find the smallest k for which: (a) for fixed n and m, we have sigma^(k)(n) > m. (b) ... J^(k)(x) = 1. (c) ... omega^(k)(n) = 1. (d) ... d^(k)(n) > m. (e) ... p(p(...(p(n)-1)...)-1)-1 = 1.

artifact.status_search_result: These iteration-depth problems for classical arithmetic functions (sigma, pi, omega, d, and the largest prime factor minus one) are long-standing questions in elementary number theory. Partial results exist (e.g. Erdős–Granville–Pomerance–Spiro type results on iterates of sigma; results on iterating pi due to Erdős and others; bounds on the "Pratt tree" depth associated with iterating p(n)-1), but no closed-form or sharp determination of the minimal iteration count is known in general, and the analogous questions for sigma_r and for primes in arithmetic progressions remain open.

status_evidence.title: Iterates of the sum-of-divisors function
status_evidence.snippet: Studies the behavior of iterates sigma^{(k)}(n), establishing growth and density results but not exact iteration counts.
status_evidence.claim: Iteration of sigma is studied with partial growth results only.

status_evidence.title: Pratt trees and the largest prime factor
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses the depth of iteration n -> p(n)-1, related to Pratt's primality proofs; only probabilistic/heuristic estimates are known.
status_evidence.claim: Depth of iterating p(n)-1 remains an open problem with only heuristic/asymptotic results.
